steps.name: Covariate structure and confounding diagnostic
caveats: n=6 per arm means PCA structure can be dominated by one sample; do not over-interpret a PC that is driven by a single point
Sex-marker checks can be ambiguous in low-depth libraries — report values rather than asserting a swap

steps.question: In the 12 adipose samples, how are sex and age distributed across the treated and control arms, and how much expression variance do condition, sex and age each explain before any differential model is fitted?
constraints: Use only the two provided input files; do not download anything
Do not drop samples in this step — flag suspicious samples for T1S2 to consider, do not remove them
Keep age continuous here; do not bin into categories
Report the retained gene count and all filter parameters explicitly
This step must not select the primary DE model — it is diagnostic and descriptive only
steps.description: Load /eval-full-32-without-covariates-n6-2/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 gene symbols x 12 samples, raw integer Salmon counts, first column = gene symbol) and /eval-full-32-without-covariates-n6-2/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows: sample, condition, sex, age). steps.name: DESeq2 treated vs control adjusted for sex and age
caveats: 6 vs 6 is modest power; a small or empty FDR<0.05 list is a real and reportable outcome, not a reason to relax the threshold

With age imbalanced across arms, part of the treatment effect and part of the age effect are collinear — adjusted log2FCs are attenuated relative to the unadjusted ones by construction, and that is the correct behaviour
If T1S1 found sex badly imbalanced across arms, the sex coefficient absorbs treatment signal for sex-linked genes; note this rather than dropping the term
Shrunken LFCs are for ranking and visualisation; p-values come from the unshrunken Wald test
steps.context: The primary scientific question is the treated-vs-control contrast. Because the user states the arms are not age-matched, the covariate-adjusted model is primary and the unadjusted model is a sensitivity check, not the other way around. DESeq2 is the right estimator here: 12,000 genes, 12 samples, raw Salmon integer counts, negative-binomial with empirical-Bayes dispersion shrinkage is well calibrated at n=6 per arm where per-gene variance estimates alone are not.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control adipose samples when sex and age are adjusted for, and how much does that gene list change if the covariates are dropped?
constraints: Design must be ~ sex + age_centred + condition with control as reference; do not swap the contrast direction
Age must enter as a centred continuous covariate — do not dichotomise it
Use the same gene filter as T1S1 so all models are compared on an identical gene set
Do not apply a log2FC cutoff when defining significance; report effect sizes separately
Do not use surrogate-variable or batch-correction methods — the design is a single batch with known covariates, and with 8 residual df there is no room for latent factors
Report exact numbers, never 'many genes changed'
steps.description: Fit the pre-specified primary model in DESeq2 on the same filtered gene set as T1S1 (count >= 10 in at least 6 samples): design ~ sex + age_centred + condition, with condition releveled so control is the reference and age mean-centred and kept continuous. Report dispersion-estimate and p-value-histogram plots, the number of genes flagged by Cook's-distance outlier filtering, and the number removed by independent filtering with the fitted filter threshold. Genes significant only in the unadjusted model are listed explicitly

steps.name: Robustness audit of the DE hits
caveats: Leave-one-out at n=12 is unstable by nature; the point is to flag fragility, not to produce a corrected p-value
A Wilcoxon test at 6 vs 6 has a minimum attainable p-value near 0.002 and cannot survive genome-wide correction — use it as a directional sanity check only
Gene symbols in the counts matrix may not all resolve against an annotation resource; report the unmapped fraction rather than dropping genes silently
steps.context: At 6 vs 6 with an age-imbalanced design, the two ways a DE list misleads are outlier-driven hits and covariate leakage. Neither is visible in a volcano plot. This step produces the evidence a reader needs to decide which hits to believe, and is deliberately separated from T1S2 so the primary statistics are not tuned in response to it.
steps.question: Are the treated-vs-control hits driven by treatment, or by sex-chromosome genes, residual age effects, or single outlier samples?
constraints: Do not modify or re-run the primary DE model to improve results — this step reports on T1S2's output, it does not replace it
Use VST values from the same filtered matrix as T1S2 for all visualisation and non-parametric testing
Name genes explicitly in the shortlist and the exclusion list; do not summarise as counts only
Match the organism when resolving any annotation resource — this is Homo sapiens (taxon 9606) data with HGNC gene symbols
steps.description: Audit the primary FDR<0.05 gene list (or, if fewer than 20 genes reach FDR<0.05, the top 50 by adjusted p-value) from T1S2. For each audited gene: (1) plot VST expression per sample coloured by condition and shaped by sex with age as a label, so single-sample-driven effects are visible; (2) compute a leave-one-sample-out re-fit of the primary DESeq2 model and report, per gene, the maximum change in log2FC and whether the gene loses FDR<0.05 when any single sample is dropped — flag every gene whose significance depends on one sample; (3) run a covariate-free Wilcoxon rank-sum test on VST values as a distribution-free cross-check, reporting the concordance in direction and how many DESeq2 hits are also nominally significant non-parametrically. acceptance_criteria: Per-gene expression plots for the audited gene set, showing condition, sex and age per sample
Leave-one-out re-fit results reported per gene, with an explicit list of genes whose FDR<0.05 status depends on a single sample
Wilcoxon cross-check reported with directional concordance and the count of DESeq2 hits that are also nominally significant
chrX/chrY membership annotated for audited genes, or an explicit statement that no chromosome annotation resource was available and the marker-panel fallback was used
Age correlation and condition-adjusted partial correlation reported per audited gene, with likely age-confounded genes named
A final ranked shortlist of hits judged robust, with the reason each excluded gene was excluded

steps.name: Rank-based pathway enrichment of the adjusted contrast
caveats: FDR<0.25 is the conventional exploratory GSEA threshold and is not evidence of a confirmed pathway effect — label these results exploratory
GO-BP parent/child sets overlap heavily; an uncollapsed count of significant terms overstates the number of independent findings
The counts matrix holds 12,000 gene symbols, a subset of the transcriptome — gene sets will be partially covered and NES is affected by that truncation; report the coverage
If the underlying DE signal is weak, GSEA will still return ranked sets — an NES without a supporting leading edge of audited genes should not be reported as a finding
steps.context: Human adipose, treated vs control. With 12 samples the thresholded DE list may be short, so a rank-based GSEA over the whole ranking is the better-powered primary enrichment readout. The environment stages MSigDB human hallmark (50 sets) and human GO BP/CC/MF collections as symbol GMTs — HGNC symbols, matching the counts matrix's gene-symbol index — so no identifier conversion should be needed beyond reporting the overlap.
steps.question: Which biological processes and hallmark programmes are coordinately shifted between treated and control adipose, using the full covariate-adjusted ranking rather than a thresholded gene list?
constraints: Use the human (Homo sapiens) hallmark and GO gene-set collections — never the mouse or rat versions
Rank on the covariate-adjusted primary contrast from T1S2, not on the unadjusted sensitivity model
Background for any over-representation test is the T1S2 tested-gene universe, not the full 12,000-row input
Set a fixed random seed for fgsea and report it

If a required human gene-set collection is not present at run time, report which one was missing and run the enrichment on whichever staged human collection is available rather than substituting another organism
steps.description: Take the complete T1S2 primary-contrast results table (all tested genes, sex+age-adjusted) and build a single ranking statistic per gene — the Wald statistic, or sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue) if the Wald statistic is unavailable — deduplicating repeated gene symbols by keeping the most extreme statistic and reporting how many duplicates were collapsed. Run fgsea (multilevel) against human hallmark gene sets and human GO Biological Process gene sets from the staged pathway references, restricted to sets of 15-500 genes after intersecting with the tested-gene universe. Report normalised enrichment scores, BH-adjusted p-values, set sizes and leading-edge gene symbols for every set at FDR<0.25, and enrichment plots for the top 10 by adjusted p-value. Because GO-BP sets are hierarchically nested and share members, collapse redundant significant GO terms (fgsea's collapsePathways or a leading-edge Jaccard cut) and report both the raw and collapsed counts. As a secondary readout only, run an over-representation test (hypergeometric, background = the tested-gene universe from T1S2, not all 12,000 rows) on the FDR<0.05 up- and down-regulated lists separately — and if fewer than 15 genes are significant in a direction, skip ORA for that direction and state why rather than running an underpowered test. acceptance_criteria: Ranking statistic construction documented, including how duplicate gene symbols were collapsed and how many
fgsea run against human hallmark and human GO-BP sets with minSize=15, maxSize=500 after intersecting with the tested universe, and the number of sets tested reported for each collection
Results table with NES, p, BH-adjusted p, set size and leading-edge symbols for all sets at FDR<0.25
Redundant GO terms collapsed, with both raw and collapsed significant counts reported
ORA run only where >=15 genes are significant in a direction, using the tested-gene universe as background, or explicitly skipped with the reason stated
Top pathway leading-edge genes cross-referenced against the T1S3 robust shortlist
Fraction of tested genes matching the gene-set universe reported

plan.title: Adipose treated vs control DE with sex/age covariates
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single bulk RNA-seq experiment: /data/inputs/counts/counts.csv, 12,000 gene symbols x 12 human adipose samples of raw Salmon-derived integer counts, with /data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv giving condition (6 treated, 6 control), sex (F/M) and age (years) per sample. The research question is a plain two-group contrast, but the user flags two nuisance structures the design does not control: sex is a strong transcriptional covariate in adipose (X/Y-linked genes especially), and the groups are NOT age-matched, so age is a potential confounder of the treatment effect rather than merely a source of noise.

T1S1 first establishes what the covariates actually do before any model is fixed: filter low-count genes, VST-transform, and quantify how much variance PCs carry from condition, sex and age, and — critically — how badly age is imbalanced between arms and whether sex is imbalanced too. With n=6 per arm and 3 model terms, degrees of freedom are scarce (12 samples - 4 coefficients = 8 residual df), so the diagnostic decides whether adjusting for age buys anything or merely burns df and collinearity with the very effect being estimated. That diagnostic is reported, not used to silently reshape the primary model.

T1S2 runs the primary DESeq2 analysis with the pre-specified design ~ sex + age + condition, treating control as the reference level, with age centred and kept continuous. The adjusted model is the primary result because the user explicitly says the arms are not age-matched: an unadjusted contrast cannot separate treatment from age. Two secondary models — ~condition alone and ~sex + condition — are run on the identical filtered gene set purely as a sensitivity comparison, so the report can state how much of the gene list depends on the covariate choice. Shrunken LFCs (apeglm) are produced for ranking. Independent filtering and BH FDR are used as DESeq2 defaults; a hard fold-change filter is not applied to define significance.

T1S3 sits between statistics and biology: it audits whether the surviving hits are simply sex-linked or age-driven genes leaking through, checks sex-chromosome genes explicitly, and re-tests the top hits with a covariate-free non-parametric check to flag any hit that is one-sample-driven. n=6 vs 6 is modest; outlier-driven hits are the dominant failure mode at this size and Cook's distance filtering alone does not surface them for the reader.

T2S1 takes the ranked statistic (not a thresholded list) into fgsea against staged human hallmark and GO-BP gene sets, because with 12 samples a rank-based enrichment is far better powered than an overlap test on a possibly-tiny significant list. It runs on the primary adjusted contrast and reports leading-edge genes so pathway calls stay traceable to individual genes.

Because GO-BP sets are hierarchically nested and share members, collapse redundant significant GO terms (fgsea's collapsePathways or a leading-edge Jaccard cut) and report both the raw and collapsed counts. As a secondary readout only, run an over-representation test (hypergeometric, background = the tested-gene universe from T1S2, not all 12,000 rows) on the FDR<0.05 up- and down-regulated lists separately — and if fewer than 15 genes are significant in a direction, skip ORA for that direction and state why rather than running an underpowered test. Cross-reference the leading-edge genes of the top pathways against the robust shortlist from T1S3 so pathway claims stay traceable to genes that survived the audit.
steps.context: Human adipose, treated vs control. With 12 samples the thresholded DE list may be short, so a rank-based GSEA over the whole ranking is the better-powered primary enrichment readout. The environment stages MSigDB human hallmark (50 sets) and human GO BP/CC/MF collections as symbol GMTs — HGNC symbols, matching the counts matrix's gene-symbol index — so no identifier conversion should be needed beyond reporting the overlap.
acceptance_criteria: Ranking statistic construction documented, including how duplicate gene symbols were collapsed and how many
fgsea run against human hallmark and human GO-BP sets with minSize=15, maxSize=500 after intersecting with the tested universe, and the number of sets tested reported for each collection
Results table with NES, p, BH-adjusted p, set size and leading-edge symbols for all sets at FDR<0.25
Redundant GO terms collapsed, with both raw and collapsed significant counts reported
ORA run only where >=15 genes are significant in a direction, using the tested-gene universe as background, or explicitly skipped with the reason stated
Top pathway leading-edge genes cross-referenced against the T1S3 robust shortlist
Fraction of tested genes matching the gene-set universe reported
constraints: Use the human (Homo sapiens) hallmark and GO gene-set collections — never the mouse or rat versions
Rank on the covariate-adjusted primary contrast from T1S2, not on the unadjusted sensitivity model
Background for any over-representation test is the T1S2 tested-gene universe, not the full 12,000-row input
Set a fixed random seed for fgsea and report it

If a required human gene-set collection is not present at run time, report which one was missing and run the enrichment on whichever staged human collection is available rather than substituting another organism
caveats: FDR<0.25 is the conventional exploratory GSEA threshold and is not evidence of a confirmed pathway effect — label these results exploratory
GO-BP parent/child sets overlap heavily; an uncollapsed count of significant terms overstates the number of independent findings
The counts matrix holds 12,000 gene symbols, a subset of the transcriptome — gene sets will be partially covered and NES is affected by that truncation; report the coverage
If the underlying DE signal is weak, GSEA will still return ranked sets — an NES without a supporting leading edge of audited genes should not be reported as a finding
